messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: multiple containers in cluster 'dedicated-eu-2' entering CrashLoopBackOff. Alert group: runtime-segfaults. Affected service: redwood-runtime. Pager: @Anya Patel on-call.

Anya Patel: on it. pulling logs now — is this hitting customer-facing pools or internal canaries?

eng-runtime-bot: Affected pools: dedicated-eu-2 (GPU), traffic routing: 85% hosted-api, 15% dedicated. Recent deploy: vllm-runtime:1.13.0 rolled 10m ago.

Devon Kim: I see repeated segfaults in the container logs: `SIGSEGV (segfault) at 0x0 ip=0x7f8c3a2b4f5d` referencing `libnvkernel_plugin.so + 0x1f5d`. Also CUDA error messages right before the segfault: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then immediate crash.

Samir Rao: that library name matches the custom TensorRT kernel plugin we landed as part of 1.13.0.

Maria Lopez: customers on dedicated pools might see failures, we should start mitigation and notify account owners. @Anya want me to open a quick status note for SRE->CS handoff?

Anya Patel: yes please. Maria, post a short note with impacted clusters and ETA for mitigation. I'll coordinate the mitigation steps.

Maria Lopez: Posted to #customer-notify-dedicated: "Dedicated EU-2 experiencing crate crashes due to runtime segfaults. We are mitigating now, ETA 30-60m. Will follow up with impacted accounts." :white_check_mark:

Devon Kim: quick triage commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide
kubectl -n runtime logs pod/redwood-runtime-5f4d7 -c runtime --tail=200 | grep -i segfault -A5
kubectl -n runtime describe pod redwood-runtime-5f4d7
```
Found repeated restarts ~ every 20s. kernel message snippet from pod logs: `terminating with signal 11 (SIGSEGV)`

Samir Rao: can we confirm if core dumps enabled? If so, grab core and run gdb to get bt. If not, next mitigation should be to disable the custom kernel path and fallback to CPU/Torch path.

Anya Patel: I'm enabling core dumps and increasing retention on the affected nodes. Devon, can you run the collector script and upload tar to the incident bucket? Use: `./tools/collect-runtime-dumps.sh --cluster dedicated-eu-2 --out /tmp/dumps.tar.gz`

Devon Kim: running it now. grabbing `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` as well. snippet: 
```
# dmesg excerpt
[  1234.567890] DeviceKernel: GPU 0: PID 27412 invoked illegal memory access
[  1234.567892] segfault at 0 ip 00007f8c3a2b4f5d sp 00007fffbad3c3f0 error 4 in libnvkernel_plugin.so[7f8c39f00000+1b000]
```
Uploading to s3://redwood-incidents/1752902400/dumps.tar.gz

eng-runtime-bot: Noted: core dump uploaded. Hash: sha256:abcd1234.

Samir Rao: while we wait for dumps, mitigation plan: A) disable custom kernel plugin via env var RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=1, then rolling restart runtime pods in dedicated-eu-2. B) Temporarily redirect traffic from dedicated-eu-2 to hosted and fallback CPU variant. C) Taint/cordon nodes with suspected GPUs to avoid further scheduling. D) Build hotfix image with plugin removed and schedule canary.

Anya Patel: agree. Devon—can you patch the runtime k8s deployment with the env var and scale rolling restart? Use this kubectl patch: 
```
kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/redwood-runtime RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=1
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/redwood-runtime
```
Also update the routing policy in the console to reduce traffic to 5% for dedicated-eu-2. Maria will coordinate customer-facing message.

Devon Kim: patch applied. rollout started. Watching pod restarts.

eng-runtime-bot: rolling restart triggered. New pods starting without plugin path. Health checks passing for new pods.

Devon Kim: new pods come up, logs show runtime starting without custom kernel, using fallback execution path. No segfaults observed in the last 2 restarts.

Anya Patel: good. I'm increasing sampling and watching latency. Expect higher token cost on fallback path — put a note on cost/temp-lift.

Maria Lopez: updated customer note: "Mitigation in progress: runtime reverted to fallback execution path for dedicated-eu-2. Some requests may see increased latency/cost. We're actively building a patched runtime image and will run canaries. Will update in 30m." 

Samir Rao: cores uploaded show crash in plugin init path. Backtrace (sanitized):
```
# gdb backtrace
#0  0x00007f8c3a2b4f5d in plugin_init() at libnvkernel_plugin.cpp:123
#1  0x00007f8c39f00123 in init_runtime() at runtime.cpp:98
#2  0x0000555555567890 in main() at main.cpp:45
```
Looks like plugin init derefs a null pointer when probing for tensor shapes in rare GPU states. Repro rate on canary nodes ~ 0/100 after disabling plugin.

Devon Kim: we still have a couple older pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff on drained nodes. I'll force delete and let node kubelet replace them.

Anya Patel: cordoning nodes to avoid scheduling until patched: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-47 dedicated=isolate:NoSchedule
```
Also flagging for infra: check kernel driver version and recent driver updates.

eng-runtime-bot: driver matrix check: nodes were on NVIDIA driver 525.116, which is supported. No recent driver upgrade in last 72h.

Samir Rao: next steps: create hotfix branch removing plugin usage, run unit tests and a small canary build. Devon, can you stand up a canary pool with the hotfix image once it's available?

Devon Kim: will do. Starting image build now: `docker build -t registry/redwood/vllm-runtime:1.13.0-hotfix-1 .` will push then deploy to canary-nodes.

Maria Lopez: CS request: compile a short impact summary we can send to customers — list of clusters, estimated window, and mitigation actions. Samir please include root cause hypothesis cautioning it's preliminary.

Samir Rao: will write a short summary for Maria. Hypothesis: bug in TensorRT custom kernel plugin causing illegal memory access under specific GPU state; triggered after 1.13.0 deploy. Not ruling out rare driver interaction.

Anya Patel: status check in 20m. Current impact: no new crashloops after disabling custom kernel, traffic reduced to 5% on dedicated-eu-2, canaries pending hotfix build. Logging increased.

eng-runtime-bot: canary build pushed: registry/redwood/vllm-runtime:1.13.0-hotfix-1. Canary deploy started on canary-nodes. Health checks: 2/3 passing (one pod still warming up).

Devon Kim: canary pods stable for 15m, no segfaults.

Anya Patel: ok prepare rollback plan and timeline to re-enable plugin after hotfix validated. Also open follow-up ticket for postmortem and test coverage for plugin init path.

Maria Lopez: customer note updated: "Hotfix in progress; canary stable. We will normalise traffic and follow with permanent patch. Expect full resolution in ~2h pending rollout verification." :thumbsup:

Samir Rao: filed GH issue #4789 with reproducible steps, attached core dump and gdb bt, assigned to eng-runtime/infra.

Devon Kim: uncordoning nodes and draining completed after pods replaced with non-plugin runtime. Nodes will be monitored.

Anya Patel: thanks all. I'll hand off to day shift in 1h with runbook steps: 1) verify no segfaults in logs for 30m 2) gradually increase traffic to dedicated-eu-2 to 50% while monitoring error-rate and latency 3) if stable, push hotfix to prod and remove RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS env var 4) if flaps reappear, rollback and open Sev2.

eng-runtime-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Root-cause: suspected plugin segfault; impact: degraded dedicated cluster and increased latency for routed traffic. Follow-up: postmortem + test coverage.

Anya Patel: handing off to day SREs: @Devon @Samir please keep 1hr on-call to support rollout. Maria, CS will continue updates. I'll update the incident board and mark as mitigated but not resolved.

Maria Lopez: added notes to incident tracker, informed account execs.

Devon Kim: :white_check_mark: monitoring shows no new crashloops for 40m.

Samir Rao: creating changelist for hotfix rollout schedule and testing checklist.

Anya Patel: closing loop later with a postmortem draft and timeline. Good job team. :raised_hands:

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to 'mitigated' state by Anya Patel at 1752902700. Reference ID: INC-2025-1752902400.
